competencies.name: Chapter 1: About Me
competencies.materi: Introducing Oneself and Others, Expressing Hobbies and Preferences, Describing People Physical Traits, Subject & Possessive Pronouns
competencies.cpRef: English for Nusantara untuk SMP/MTs Kelas VII — Chapter 1

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 15-18 'Galang from Kalimantan'), Galang introduces himself: 'Hello, my name is Galang. I am 13 years old. I live in Kalimantan.' What expression is used by Galang to state his age?
options: 'I am 13 years old.'
'My name is Galang.'
'I live in Kalimantan.'
'I like playing basketball.'

why.0: The phrase 'I am 13 years old' is the standard self-introduction expression used to state one's age.

distractorWhy.1: 'My name is Galang' states his identity name.
distractorWhy.2: 'I live in Kalimantan' states his origin/residence.
distractorWhy.3: 'I like playing basketball' states his hobby.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 22 Language Focus), choose the correct subject pronoun to complete the sentence: 'Monita loves reading novels. ___ goes to the library every Wednesday.'
options: She
He
They
It

why.0: Monita is a female singular proper noun, so the appropriate subject pronoun is 'She'.

distractorWhy.1: 'He' is used for male singular subjects.
distractorWhy.2: 'They' is used for plural subjects.
distractorWhy.3: 'It' is used for non-human objects or animals.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 28 Unit 2 'I Love Fishing'), Andre says: 'I like fishing because it is relaxing.' What is Andre's favorite hobby?
options: Fishing
Swimming
Playing football
Cycling

why.0: The text directly states Andre's preference: 'I like fishing'.

distractorWhy.1: Swimming is not mentioned as Andre's main hobby.
distractorWhy.2: Football is Galang's hobby in Unit 1.
distractorWhy.3: Cycling is not specified in Andre's text.

items.prompt:
Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 35 Language Focus - Possessive Adjectives), complete the dialogue correctly:
Made: 'Is this ___ bicycle, Galang?'
Galang: 'Yes, it is my bicycle.'
options: your
his
her
their

why.0: Made is directly addressing Galang (second person 'you'), so the possessive adjective is 'your'.

distractorWhy.1: 'his' refers to a third-person male.
distractorWhy.2: 'her' refers to a third-person female.
distractorWhy.3: 'their' refers to third-person plural.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 38 Unit 3 'My Friends and I'), which adjective best describes someone who wears glasses and has curly hair?
options: 'He wears glasses and has short curly hair.'
'He is tall with blue eyes.'
'He has long straight blonde hair.'
'He is short with no hair.'

why.0: The sentence 'He wears glasses and has short curly hair' accurately describes physical features of hair type and eyewear.

distractorWhy.1: Does not mention glasses or hair texture.
distractorWhy.2: Contradicts 'curly' with 'straight'.
distractorWhy.3: Contradicts having hair.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 42 Unit 1 Review), what is the appropriate greeting when meeting someone for the first time in a formal setting?
options: 'Nice to meet you.'
'See you later!'
'Good night, sleep well.'
'What's up, dude?'

why.0: 'Nice to meet you' is the standard polite expression when introduced to someone for the first time.

distractorWhy.1: 'See you later' is a leave-taking expression.
distractorWhy.2: 'Good night' is a bedtime leave-taking expression.
distractorWhy.3: 'What's up, dude?' is informal slang.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 45), fill in the correct form of verb 'to be': 'Galang and his classmates ___ excited about the school scout camp.'
options: are
is
am
was

why.0: 'Galang and his classmates' form a plural subject in simple present tense, requiring the plural verb 'are'.

distractorWhy.1: 'is' is only used for singular subjects (he/she/it).
distractorWhy.2: 'am' is only used with first person 'I'.
distractorWhy.3: 'was' is past tense.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 12), what question should you ask to find out someone's origin or hometown?
options: 'Where are you from?'
'What is your favorite color?'
'How old are you?'
'What is your hobby?'

why.0: 'Where are you from?' is the standard question used to inquire about origin or home town.

distractorWhy.1: Asks about color preference.
distractorWhy.2: Asks about age.
distractorWhy.3: Asks about activities/hobbies.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 30), complete the sentence with correct possessive pronoun: 'I have a new cat. ___ fur is white and soft.'
options: Its
It's
His
Their

why.0: 'Its' (without apostrophe) is the possessive adjective for animals or non-human entities.

distractorWhy.1: 'It's' is a contraction of 'It is' or 'It has'.
distractorWhy.2: 'His' is for human males.
distractorWhy.3: 'Their' is for plural entities.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 48), read the short text: 'Pipit likes drawing comic characters. She draws every afternoon after finishing her homework.' What can be inferred about Pipit?
options: Pipit is a disciplined student who manages her time well before pursuing her hobby
Pipit neglects her school homework to draw comics
Pipit does not enjoy drawing comics
Pipit draws comics at school during class hours

why.0: The phrase 'after finishing her homework' indicates she prioritizes school work before drawing, showing discipline.

distractorWhy.1: Contradicts the text which says she finishes homework first.
distractorWhy.2: Contradicts 'likes drawing comic characters'.
distractorWhy.3: Text specifies 'every afternoon', not during school hours.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 18), what is the opposite of the physical trait adjective 'tall'?
options: Short
Fat
Slim
Young

why.0: The antonym of 'tall' (tinggi) in physical descriptions is 'short' (pendek).

distractorWhy.1: 'Fat' is the opposite of 'thin/slim'.
distractorWhy.2: 'Slim' is the opposite of 'chubby/fat'.
distractorWhy.3: 'Young' is the opposite of 'old'.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 32), complete the expression of leave-taking: 'Good bye, Sinta! ___'
options: 'See you tomorrow!'
'I am fine, thank you.'
'My name is Sinta.'
'Nice to meet you.'

why.0: 'See you tomorrow!' is a standard leave-taking response that pairs naturally with 'Good bye'.

distractorWhy.1: 'I am fine' responds to 'How are you?'.
distractorWhy.2: 'My name is' is for introduction.
distractorWhy.3: 'Nice to meet you' is used upon initial greeting.

competencies.name: Chapter 2: Culinary and Me
competencies.materi: Describing Foods & Drinks (Taste & Texture), Recipe Procedural Text Analysis, Imperative Verbs & Cooking Steps
competencies.cpRef: English for Nusantara untuk SMP/MTs Kelas VII — Chapter 2

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 63 (Unit 1 Section 2, Worksheet 2.4), what does Monita love to eat for snacks?
options: Banana fritters
Fried rice
Fried fish
Cassava chips

why.0: Monita explicitly states in the dialogue that she loves banana fritters for snacks.

distractorWhy.1: Fried rice is Galang's favorite main meal for breakfast, not Monita's snack preference.
distractorWhy.2: Fried fish is mentioned as a main dish option during family meals, not Monita's chosen snack in the text.
distractorWhy.3: Cassava chips are mentioned in Unit 2 language focus exercises, not Monita's favorite snack in Unit 1.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 67 (Unit 1 Section 3, Worksheet 2.6), which food or drink item matches the taste descriptor "sour"?
options: Lime juice
Honey
Fried chicken
Black coffee

why.0: Lime juice has a characteristic citrus taste described as sour in the sensory vocabulary lesson.

distractorWhy.1: Honey tastes sweet, which represents a sugary flavor profile rather than sour.
distractorWhy.2: Fried chicken tastes savory or salty, describing a seasoned savory dish.
distractorWhy.3: Black coffee tastes bitter due to roasted beans, not sour.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 68 (Unit 1 Section 4, Picture 2.2), how is the texture of crackers (kerupuk) described?
options: Crunchy
Soft
Chewy
Greasy

why.0: Crackers (kerupuk) have a crisp and hard texture that makes a crisp noise when bitten, described as crunchy.

distractorWhy.1: Soft describes foods like sponge cake or steamed bread that yield easily to pressure.
distractorWhy.2: Chewy describes elastic textures like boba or rubbery meat that require repeated mastication.
distractorWhy.3: Greasy describes oily cooked foods like deep-fried chicken rather than dry crackers.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 70 (Unit 1 Section 5), which expression is used to ask about the taste of a food item?
options: What does it taste like?
Where do you cook it?
How much is the food?
When do you eat it?

why.0: "What does it taste like?" is the standard target expression given in Section 5 to inquire about flavor profiles.

distractorWhy.1: "Where do you cook it?" asks for location rather than sensory flavor details.
distractorWhy.2: "How much is the food?" asks for price rather than taste qualities.
distractorWhy.3: "When do you eat it?" asks for temporal schedule rather than food flavor.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII pages 61-62 (Comic strip 2.1), what can be inferred about Galang's breakfast habit?
options: He eats fried rice and drinks sweet tea at home.
He buys donuts and orange juice at school.
He eats banana fritters and drinks plain water for lunch.
He skips breakfast and only eats snacks at noon.

why.0: In Comic strip 2.1, Galang eats fried rice and drinks sweet tea for breakfast before going to school.

distractorWhy.1: Donuts and orange juice are not Galang's breakfast meal depicted in Comic strip 2.1.
distractorWhy.2: Banana fritters are snack items, and Galang's morning drink is sweet tea rather than plain water for lunch.
distractorWhy.3: Galang does not skip breakfast; he explicitly discusses his home breakfast meal with Monita.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 60 (Unit 1 Section 1.b), which of the following is categorized as a main meal?
options: Nasi goreng
Cassava chips
Iced tea
Banana fritters

why.0: Nasi goreng (fried rice) is categorized as a main meal because it serves as a staple substantial dish for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

distractorWhy.1: Cassava chips are categorized under snacks rather than a main meal.
distractorWhy.2: Iced tea is categorized under beverages/drinks.
distractorWhy.3: Banana fritters are categorized under light afternoon snacks.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 74 (Unit 1 Section 7, Picture 2.4), how does the speaker describe Nasi Goreng?
options: It is savory and a bit greasy.
It is sweet and very crunchy.
It is bitter and dry.
It is sour and sticky.

why.0: The text on page 74 explicitly quotes: "My favorite meal is Nasi Goreng. It's savory. It's a bit greasy."

distractorWhy.1: Sweet and crunchy describes desserts like sugar-coated snacks or crackers, not fried rice.
distractorWhy.2: Bitter and dry contradicts the savory taste and moist/oily texture of fried rice.
distractorWhy.3: Sour and sticky describes fermented or acidic dishes, not standard savory fried rice.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 75 (Unit 2 Section 2.b), what is Galang's favorite snack?
options: Banana fritters
Chocolate cake
Pecel
Rujak

why.0: The text titled "Galang's Favorite Snack" begins with the sentence: "My favorite snack is banana fritters."

distractorWhy.1: Chocolate cake is Monita's baking project text on page 77.
distractorWhy.2: Pecel is a traditional vegetable dish featured in Section 4 (page 79).
distractorWhy.3: Rujak is a fruit dish loved by Monita's mother in Section 4 (page 80).

items.prompt: Based on the passage "Galang's Favorite Snack" on page 75, how are the textures of banana fritters described?
options: Crispy and crunchy outside, sweet and soft inside.
Soft and wet outside, salty and hard inside.
Hard and tough outside, sour and cold inside.
Chewy and greasy outside, bitter and dry inside.

why.0: The text states: "I like them because they are crispy and crunchy outside, but sweet and soft inside."

distractorWhy.1: Soft and wet outside contradicts the fried crispness specified in the passage.
distractorWhy.2: Hard and tough outside mischaracterizes fried batter and warm bananas.
distractorWhy.3: Chewy and bitter contradicts the crisp outer batter and sweet interior.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 77 (Unit 2 Section 3.b, Picture 2.6), what toppings are used on Monita's Black Forest cake?
options: Whipped cream and cherries
Palm sugar and grated coconut
Peanut sauce and chili powder
Sprinkles and fried shallots

why.0: Monita's Black Forest cake post highlights whipped cream frosting topped with cherries.

distractorWhy.1: Palm sugar and grated coconut are traditional toppings for Indonesian traditional sweets like klepon or lupis.
distractorWhy.2: Peanut sauce and chili powder are savory dressings for dishes like Pecel or Rujak.
distractorWhy.3: Fried shallots are savory garnishes used for fried rice or soups.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII pages 79-80 (Unit 2 Section 4), what key difference distinguishes Pecel from Rujak in their dressing and main ingredients?
options: Pecel uses peanut sauce over boiled vegetables, while Rujak uses spicy palm sugar over sliced fruits.
Pecel uses palm sugar over raw meat, while Rujak uses coconut milk over cooked rice.
Pecel is an iced sweet dessert, while Rujak is a warm bakery product.
Pecel uses mayonnaise over seafood, while Rujak uses soy sauce over noodles.

why.0: The reading mind maps specify Pecel as boiled vegetables with peanut sauce, and Rujak as sliced fruits with spicy palm sugar dressing.

distractorWhy.1: Neither dish contains raw meat or coconut milk base for cooked rice.
distractorWhy.2: Pecel and Rujak are traditional Indonesian fresh/boiled salad dishes, not bakery products or ice cream.
distractorWhy.3: Mayonnaise seafood and soy sauce noodles misrepresent these traditional fruit and vegetable dishes.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 81 (Unit 2 Section 5 Language Focus), complete the sentence: "Monita needs ___ oven to bake the cake."
options: an
a
some
many

why.0: The word "oven" begins with a vowel sound /ɒ/, requiring the indefinite article "an".

distractorWhy.1: The article "a" is used before singular countable nouns beginning with consonant sounds.
distractorWhy.2: "Some" is used with plural or uncountable nouns, whereas "oven" is a singular countable noun.
distractorWhy.3: "Many" is a quantifier used with plural countable nouns, not singular nouns.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 81 (Unit 2 Section 5, Worksheet 2.17), which article correctly completes sentence 7: "Monita's father makes ___ plate of fried rice for breakfast."
options: a
an
some
these

why.0: The word "plate" starts with the consonant sound /p/, so it takes the indefinite article "a".

distractorWhy.1: "an" is only used before words starting with vowel sounds.
distractorWhy.2: "some" is inappropriate here because "plate" is a singular countable noun preceded by a quantity marker.
distractorWhy.3: "these" is a plural demonstrative determiner, which cannot modify the singular noun "plate".

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII pages 83-84 (Unit 3 Section 2), which utensil is used to stir or flip food in a frying pan/wok?
options: spatula
napkin
chopstick
glass

why.0: A spatula is the flat cooking tool designed for stirring, lifting, and flipping ingredients in a pan or wok.

distractorWhy.1: A napkin is a piece of cloth or paper used for wiping mouth and hands during eating.
distractorWhy.2: Chopsticks are handheld eating utensils used primarily for picking up food pieces.
distractorWhy.3: A glass is a drink container, not a cooking utensil used in a wok.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 84 (Unit 3 Section 2.c, Worksheet 2.19), which action verb correctly completes the phrase: "I ___ the vegetable into small pieces"?
options: cut
heat
pour
turn on

why.0: The action verb "cut" means dividing food into smaller parts using a knife.

distractorWhy.1: "heat" applies to liquids or oil in a cooking vessel.
distractorWhy.2: "pour" applies to liquids like water or oil transferred into containers.
distractorWhy.3: "turn on" applies to appliances like the stove.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 87 (Unit 3 Section 4.a, Recipe for Traditional Fried Rice), what should you do right after heating cooking oil in the pan?
options: Put the eggs into the pan and stir/scramble them.
Add a pinch of salt to the cold pan.
Serve the fried rice on a plate immediately.
Chop the raw rice into pieces.

why.0: According to the recipe steps on page 87, Step 3 is heating oil, followed by Step 4: "Put the eggs into the pan" and Step 5: "Stir the egg and scramble it."

distractorWhy.1: Salt is added later as step 8 for seasoning after cooked rice is added.
distractorWhy.2: Serving the dish is the final step after all cooking is complete.
distractorWhy.3: Cooked rice is added whole in step 7, not chopped raw.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII pages 88-89 (Unit 3 Section 4.c-d, Table 2.3 & 2.4), what are the main structural components of a procedural recipe text?
options: Goal, Materials (utensils & ingredients), and Steps
Orientation, Complication, and Resolution
Thesis, Arguments, and Reiteration
Identification and Description

why.0: Table 2.3 defines procedural recipe text structure as: Goal (aim), Materials (ingredients and utensils), and Steps (ordered instructions).

distractorWhy.1: Orientation, Complication, and Resolution form the structure of narrative texts.
distractorWhy.2: Thesis, Arguments, and Reiteration form the structure of analytical exposition texts.
distractorWhy.3: Identification and Description form the structure of descriptive texts.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 90 (Unit 3 Section 5 Language Focus), how is a positive imperative sentence formed in English cooking instructions?
options: By using the base verb without a subject at the beginning of the sentence.
By starting with "You must to" followed by a past tense verb.
By placing an auxiliary verb "Did" before a subject.
By using an -ing verb with a subject pronoun.

why.0: Section 5 explicitly states that imperative sentences use the base verb with no subject (e.g., "Heat the oil in the pan").

distractorWhy.1: "You must to" is grammatically incorrect and does not follow imperative command structure.
distractorWhy.2: "Did" creates past tense questions, not direct imperative instructions.
distractorWhy.3: Subject pronouns with -ing verbs form continuous tenses, not imperative commands.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII page 90 (Unit 3 Section 5 Language Focus), which sentence is a correct example of a negative imperative command?
options: Don't put chili in the fried rice.
Not putting chili in the fried rice.
You don't putting chili in fried rice.
No put chili in fried rice.

why.0: Negative imperative sentences follow the structure "Don't" + base verb, as shown in the textbook example "Don't put chili in the fried rice."

distractorWhy.1: "Not putting" lacks the mandatory auxiliary verb "Do" in negative imperative construction.
distractorWhy.2: "You don't putting" contains redundant subject inclusion and ungrammatical verb form.
distractorWhy.3: "No put" is non-standard broken English that violates English imperative rules.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII pages 88 and 92 (Unit 3 Section 4.c & Section 6.b), which set of temporal conjunctions is used to indicate the chronological order of cooking steps?
options: First, second, then, next, finally
Because, although, unless, since
However, nevertheless, on the other hand
Whereas, despite, in addition to

why.0: The text highlights sequence markers (conjunctions) such as first, second, then, next, and finally to order procedural steps.

distractorWhy.1: Because, although, unless, and since are causal and conditional conjunctions, not sequential markers.
distractorWhy.2: However, nevertheless, and on the other hand are contrastive transition words.
distractorWhy.3: Whereas, despite, and in addition to are contrastive and additive connectors, not order indicators.

competencies.name: Chapter 3: Home Sweet Home
competencies.materi: Rooms & Furniture in a House, Describing House Chores & Cleaning Activities, Prepositions of Place (in, on, under, next to), Rules and Abilities (can/can't)
competencies.cpRef: English for Nusantara untuk SMP/MTs Kelas VII — Chapter 3

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (pages 105-110 Unit 1 'My House'), which room is primarily used for cooking meals and preparing drinks?
options: Kitchen
Bedroom
Bathroom
Living room

why.0: The kitchen is the room in a house dedicated to cooking and food preparation.

distractorWhy.1: Bedroom is for sleeping.
distractorWhy.2: Bathroom is for bathing.
distractorWhy.3: Living room is for family gathering.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 115 Prepositions of Place), look at the sentence: 'Galang puts his school bag ___ the desk in his bedroom.' What is the correct preposition?
options: on
under
behind
in

why.0: 'on' is used when an object is supported by a flat horizontal surface (on the desk).

distractorWhy.1: under means beneath.
distractorWhy.2: behind means at the back.
distractorWhy.3: in means inside an enclosed space.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 120 Unit 2 'House Chores'), what expression describes Monita's daily cleaning activity of using a broom on the floor?
options: 'She sweeps the floor.'
'She washes the dishes.'
'She waters the plants.'
'She irons the clothes.'

why.0: 'sweeps the floor' (menyapu lantai) is the chore associated with a broom.

distractorWhy.1: Washing dishes is for plates/cups.
distractorWhy.2: Watering plants is for garden.
distractorWhy.3: Ironing clothes is for garments.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 128 Language Focus - Modals for Rules), choose the correct sentence to state a household rule about cleanliness:
options: 'We must keep our bedroom clean and tidy.'
'We can throw trash on the floor.'
'We cannot sleep at night.'
'We must break the window.'

why.0: 'must keep our bedroom clean' states a positive house rule requirement.

distractorWhy.1: Contradicts cleanliness rules.
distractorWhy.2: Illogical rule.
distractorWhy.3: Destructive behavior.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 112), what piece of furniture is typically found in the living room for people to sit comfortably?
options: Sofa
Stove
Refrigerator
Wardrobe

why.0: A sofa is comfortable seating furniture in a living room.

distractorWhy.1: Stove is in the kitchen.
distractorWhy.2: Refrigerator is for food cold storage.
distractorWhy.3: Wardrobe is in bedroom for clothes.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 132 Unit 3 Review), complete the sentence with 'can' or 'can't': 'Sinta ___ cook fried rice because her mother taught her last week.'
options: can
can't
must not
should not

why.0: 'can' expresses learned ability/capability in the present.

distractorWhy.1: can't expresses inability.
distractorWhy.2: must not expresses prohibition.
distractorWhy.3: should not expresses negative advice.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 114), which preposition completes the sentence: 'The cat is sleeping ___ the bed.'
options: under
between
inside of
through

why.0: 'under' (di bawah) is the correct preposition showing the cat's sleeping spot beneath the bed frame.

distractorWhy.1: between requires two objects.
distractorWhy.2: inside of is inside mattress.
distractorWhy.3: through implies motion.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 122), what is the household chore expression for washing dirty dishes and spoons in the sink?
options: 'Wash the dishes'
'Make the bed'
'Clean the window'
'Mop the floor'

why.0: 'Wash the dishes' (mencuci piring) is the chore for cleaning eating utensils.

distractorWhy.1: Make the bed is tidying blankets.
distractorWhy.2: Clean the window is glass cleaning.
distractorWhy.3: Mop the floor is floor cleaning.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 126), complete the sentence: 'Galang ___ play video games after finishing his homework.'
options: can
can't
must not
should not

why.0: 'can' expresses permission granted after completing duties.

distractorWhy.1: can't expresses refusal.
distractorWhy.2: must not is prohibition.
distractorWhy.3: should not is advice.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 130), what room is used for taking a shower and brushing teeth?
options: Bathroom
Dining room
Garage
Terrace

why.0: The bathroom is the designated room for personal hygiene and bathing.

distractorWhy.1: Dining room is for eating.
distractorWhy.2: Garage is for vehicles.
distractorWhy.3: Terrace is outdoor porch.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 118), where do people park their cars and motorcycles at home?
options: Garage
Living room
Attic
Balcony

why.0: The garage is the enclosed room/area used for parking vehicles.

distractorWhy.1: Living room is indoor seating.
distractorWhy.2: Attic is under roof storage.
distractorWhy.3: Balcony is upper level floor.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VII (page 134 Review), why is it important for family members to share house chores?
options: To make the house clean faster and foster cooperation among family members
To make one person do all the hard work alone
To ruin the house furniture
To increase electricity bills

why.0: Sharing chores teaches teamwork and keeps the living environment clean efficiently.

distractorWhy.1: Unfair single workload.
distractorWhy.2: Not intended to ruin furniture.
distractorWhy.3: Chores do not aim to raise bills.

competencies.name: Chapter 1: Celebrating Independence Day
competencies.materi: Describing Past Independence Day Events, Recount Text Structure, Simple Past Tense (Regular & Irregular Verbs), Past Time Connectors
competencies.cpRef: English for Nusantara untuk SMP/MTs Kelas VII — Chapter 1 (Kelas VIII)

items.prompt: Based on the dialogue between Galang and his father in Unit 1 (page 15), what game did Galang win during the school's Independence Day celebration?
options: Marble in spoon race
Tug of war
Sack race
Panjat Pinang

why.0: In the dialogue, Galang explicitly tells his father, 'I won the marble in spoon race.'

distractorWhy.1: Galang mentions tug of war as one of the games held at school, but he did not win it.
distractorWhy.2: Galang mentions sack race as one of the school activities, but he did not win this event.
distractorWhy.3: Panjat Pinang was the game joined by Galang's father when he was young, not Galang.

items.prompt: Based on Pak Rahmansyah's experience in Panjat Pinang (Unit 1, page 18), what was the first strategy his team used to overcome the slippery tree?
options: Making a human ladder and wiping off the grease bit by bit
Throwing the prizes directly from the ground with ropes
Using a long bamboo ladder brought from home
Asking the event committee to clean the whole tree first

why.0: Pak Rahmansyah explains that his team made a human ladder and wiped off the grease bit by bit to allow a climber to reach the top.

distractorWhy.1: The climber threw prizes down after reaching the top, not from the ground.
distractorWhy.2: Pak Rahmansyah's team built a human ladder using their own bodies, not a bamboo ladder.
distractorWhy.3: The team wiped off the grease themselves step by step rather than relying on the committee.

items.prompt: In recount texts describing past events (Unit 1, page 20), regular past simple verbs are formed by adding '-d', '-ed', or '-ied' to the base verb. Which group contains ONLY regular past simple verbs from Chapter 1?
options: celebrated, watched, pushed, grabbed
won, held, ate, fell
gave, made, threw, came
ran, led, beat, spoke

why.0: The verbs 'celebrated', 'watched', 'pushed', and 'grabbed' all end with the regular past suffix '-ed' or '-d'.

distractorWhy.1: The verbs 'won', 'held', 'ate', and 'fell' are all irregular past simple verbs.
distractorWhy.2: The verbs 'gave', 'made', 'threw', and 'came' change root vowels or endings irregularly.
distractorWhy.3: The verbs 'ran', 'led', 'beat', and 'spoke' are irregular past forms.

items.prompt: Based on the simple past tense rules in Unit 1 (page 20), what is the correct past form (V2) of the irregular verb 'win' to complete this sentence: 'Galang ___ the marble in spoon race yesterday'?
options: won
winned
winning
wins

why.0: The verb 'win' is an irregular verb whose past simple form is 'won'.

distractorWhy.1: The form 'winned' is incorrect because 'win' does not take the regular '-ed' ending.
distractorWhy.2: The form 'winning' is a present participle / gerund, not a simple past verb.
distractorWhy.3: The form 'wins' is a third-person singular present simple verb.

items.prompt: Complete Pak Rahmansyah's statement about reaching the prizes in Panjat Pinang using the correct Simple Past Tense verb (Unit 1, page 18): 'One of us finally got to the top and ___ the prizes to the ground.'
options: threw
throwed
throws
throwing

why.0: The past simple tense of the irregular verb 'throw' is 'threw'.

distractorWhy.1: The form 'throwed' is non-standard because 'throw' forms its past tense irregularly.
distractorWhy.2: The form 'throws' represents simple present tense third-person singular.
distractorWhy.3: The form 'throwing' is a continuous form requiring an auxiliary verb.

items.prompt: In Unit 2 (page 29), Andre talks about his experience in the Krupuk race: 'I beat Galang in the Krupuk race.' Galang replies: 'Yeah, I came second.' How did Galang finish in the Krupuk race?
options: He finished in second place.
He won first place.
He was disqualified from the race.
He did not participate in the race.

why.0: Galang explicitly states 'I came second', meaning he earned second place behind Andre.

distractorWhy.1: Andre won first place by beating Galang.
distractorWhy.2: There is no mention of disqualification in the comic strip.
distractorWhy.3: Galang actively participated and reached the final stage of the competition.

items.prompt: Based on Andre's recount text 'A Parade in My Hometown' (Unit 2, page 31), what traditional musical instruments accompanied the people marching in the second line of the parade?
options: Angklung, suling, and rebana
Drums, trumpets, and electric guitars
Gamelan, kulintang, and piano
Violin, flute, and saxophone

why.0: The text specifically mentions that singing was accompanied by traditional instruments like angklung, suling, and rebana.

distractorWhy.1: Drums, trumpets, and electric guitars are modern western instruments not listed in Andre's story.
distractorWhy.2: Gamelan, kulintang, and piano are not mentioned in this section of the text.
distractorWhy.3: Violin, flute, and saxophone are orchestra instruments not specified in the reading passage.

items.prompt: Why did Andre only watch the parade from his front yard with his father when he was a child, instead of joining it? (Unit 2, page 31)
options: Because he was too shy to join the parade
Because children were forbidden to participate
Because he did not own a bicycle
Because he was sick during Independence Day

why.0: Andre explains in his recount: 'I always wanted to join the parade but I was too shy.'

distractorWhy.1: Children actively participated by riding decorated bicycles in the parade.
distractorWhy.2: Owning a bicycle was not a requirement to march in the parade.
distractorWhy.3: The text does not state that Andre was sick on Independence Day.

items.prompt: Based on the reading text 'SMP Merdeka's School Parade' (Unit 2, page 32-33), what did Galang and his friends wear for the parade?
options: Indonesian freedom fighters' costumes and red-and-white attributes
Traditional sports jerseys with gold medals
Scary ghost costumes and dark masks
Formal school uniforms with black ties

why.0: The text states that students dressed up like Indonesian freedom fighters and wore red and white attributes.

distractorWhy.1: They wore freedom fighter costumes, not sports jerseys.
distractorWhy.2: Ghost costumes were mentioned in Andre's hometown parade, not SMP Merdeka's school parade.
distractorWhy.3: The participants wore thematic parade costumes rather than standard daily uniforms.

items.prompt: In Unit 2 Language Focus (page 36), time connectives are used to connect past events in sequence. Which time connective is specifically categorized under the ENDING group?
options: Finally
In the beginning
First of all
First

why.0: 'Finally' is listed in Table 1.2 under the Ending category to signal the final event of a story.

distractorWhy.1: 'In the beginning' belongs to the Beginning category of time connectives.
distractorWhy.2: 'First of all' is used to introduce the initial event of a recount.
distractorWhy.3: 'First' is an introductory connective marking the start of a sequence.

items.prompt: Read the sentence from Monita's blog: '___, after the rain stopped, we gathered back at the schoolyard. The headmaster announced the winner.' (Unit 2, page 39). Which time connective best fits the blank to indicate the concluding stage?
options: Finally
First of all
In the beginning
Before

why.0: 'Finally' introduces the ultimate resolution and ending phase after the rain delay.

distractorWhy.1: 'First of all' introduces the start of an event, which is inappropriate at the conclusion.
distractorWhy.2: 'In the beginning' marks the opening context rather than the final announcement.
distractorWhy.3: 'Before' requires a dependent clause or noun phrase to show temporal priority.

items.prompt: In Monita's blog about her school parade (Unit 2, page 39), who did Monita dress up as during the event?
options: Cut Nyak Dien
Tuanku Imam Bonjol
R.A. Kartini
Pattimura

why.0: Monita explicitly writes: 'I was chosen as the class representative. I dressed as Cut Nyak Dien.'

distractorWhy.1: Tuanku Imam Bonjol was the hero costume worn by a student from another class who won best costume.
distractorWhy.2: R.A. Kartini is an Indonesian national heroine, but Monita did not dress up as her.
distractorWhy.3: Pattimura is a national hero from Maluku, not the costume chosen by Monita.

items.prompt: Why did Monita and her schoolmates run back to their classroom in the middle of the school parade? (Unit 2, page 39)
options: Because it suddenly started to rain
Because the marching band stopped playing music
Because the headmaster called an urgent assembly
Because they needed to change their costumes

why.0: Monita explains: 'Suddenly, it started to rain. We ran back to our classroom.'

distractorWhy.1: The marching band was playing during the parade, but rain was the reason they ran back.
distractorWhy.2: The headmaster spoke at the schoolyard after the rain stopped, not during the parade.
distractorWhy.3: The students had already prepared and worn their costumes before marching.

items.prompt: According to Monita's recount text in Unit 3 (page 43), how many bites did Monita need to finish her krupuk and beat Galang in the final krupuk race?
options: Three or four bites
One single bite
Ten bites
Seven or eight bites

why.0: Monita notes in her story: 'I finished my krupuk with three or four bites.'

distractorWhy.1: One bite was mentioned as a caption in a fun time game, but not in Monita's actual race text.
distractorWhy.2: Ten bites would be too slow to win a krupuk race.
distractorWhy.3: Seven or eight bites is inaccurate based on Monita's written recount.

items.prompt: In Unit 3 (page 43), what happened to Andre during the sack race competition?
options: He led the race at first, but fell in the middle and finished second
He won first place without any trouble
He withdrew from the race due to an injury
He came third behind Pipit's team

why.0: Monita recounts: 'At first, he led the race, but suddenly he fell in the middle of the race. But finally, he came second.'

distractorWhy.1: Andre did not win first place because he fell midway through the race.
distractorWhy.2: Andre completed the race despite falling and managed to earn second place.
distractorWhy.3: Pipit's team came third in the tandem race, not the sack race.

items.prompt: Based on the Recount Text Structure explained in Unit 3 (page 45), what is the main purpose of the 'Orientation' section?
options: To set the context by providing background information about who, where, and when the events occurred
To present a sequence of events in chronological order
To give step-by-step instructions on how to play a game
To state a personal conclusion or feeling about the events

why.0: Table 1.3 defines Orientation as setting the context and providing background details regarding who, where, and when.

distractorWhy.1: Recording events in chronological order is the function of the Events section.
distractorWhy.2: Giving step-by-step instructions is the structure of a procedure text, not recount orientation.
distractorWhy.3: Stating personal feelings or conclusions is the function of Re-orientation.

items.prompt: Read the final paragraph of Monita's story (Unit 3, page 43): 'It was a joyful day at my school. Everyone put a smile on their faces. I was delighted. At the end of the event, my class was announced as the grand champion of the whole competition.' Which structural element of recount text does this paragraph illustrate? (Unit 3, page 45)
options: Re-orientation
Orientation
Events
Identification

why.0: Re-orientation summarizes the writer's personal feelings, comments, and the overall outcome of the experience.

distractorWhy.1: Orientation appears at the beginning to set context (who, where, when).
distractorWhy.2: Events detail the specific series of actions that occurred during the day.
distractorWhy.3: Identification is part of descriptive text structure, not recount text structure.

items.prompt: Identify the sentence that uses correct Simple Past Tense irregular verbs based on the recount text in Chapter 1:
options: Monita felt happy because her class won the grand champion title.
Monita feel happy because her class winned the grand champion title.
Monita feeled happy because her class win the grand champion title.
Monita feeling happy because her class wins the grand champion title.

why.0: The irregular past simple form of 'feel' is 'felt' and the irregular past simple form of 'win' is 'won'.

distractorWhy.1: 'feel' is present tense and 'winned' is an incorrect regularized form of 'win'.
distractorWhy.2: 'feeled' is incorrect because 'feel' is irregular, and 'win' is base form.
distractorWhy.3: 'feeling' lacks a past auxiliary verb and 'wins' is present tense.

items.prompt: In Unit 1 (page 20), how is an interrogative sentence (question) correctly structured in Simple Past Tense when asking about past participation?
options: Did you participate in the krupuk race yesterday?
Did you participated in the krupuk race yesterday?
Were you participate in the krupuk race yesterday?
Do you participated in the krupuk race yesterday?

why.0: The rule for simple past questions is 'Did + subject + base verb (V1)', so 'participate' stays in base form after 'Did'.

distractorWhy.1: Using 'participated' (V2) after auxiliary 'Did' creates a double past tense error.
distractorWhy.2: 'Were' cannot function as an auxiliary verb before a base action verb like 'participate'.
distractorWhy.3: 'Do' is present tense auxiliary, which conflicts with past tense context.

items.prompt: In Unit 2 (page 36 Table 1.2), time connectives are categorized into Beginning, Middle, and Ending. Which time connective belongs to the MIDDLE category?
options: After that
In the beginning
First of all
In the end

why.0: 'After that' is listed in Table 1.2 under Middle time connectives to show sequence between past events.

distractorWhy.1: 'In the beginning' belongs to the Beginning category of time connectives.
distractorWhy.2: 'First of all' belongs to the Beginning category used to start a recount.
distractorWhy.3: 'In the end' belongs to the Ending category of time connectives.

competencies.name: Chapter 2: Kindness Begins with Me
competencies.materi: Reading Narrative Texts & Fables, Moral Values of Kindness, Narrative Structure (Orientation, Complication, Resolution), Direct & Indirect Speech
competencies.cpRef: English for Nusantara untuk SMP/MTs Kelas VII — Chapter 2 (Kelas VIII)

items.prompt: Berdasarkan cerita The Ugly Duckling Part 1 pada Chapter 2 Unit 1 (halaman 97-101), bagaimana sikap Mother Duck ketika telur kelima menetas dan menghasilkan seekor anak bebek berwarna abu-abu yang berbeda dari empat anak bebek kuning lainnya?
options: Mother Duck tetap menenangkan anak bebek abu-abu itu dengan menyebutnya berbeda, berwarna abu-abu, dan pemberani.
Mother Duck langsung mengusir anak bebek abu-abu tersebut keluar dari sarang.
Mother Duck marah dan menolak mengakui telur kelima yang menetas.
Mother Duck mengabaikan anak bebek abu-abu itu dan membiarkannya sendirian di kolam.

why.0: Dalam teks cerita Ugly Duckling Part 1, Mother Duck berusaha menenangkan anak bebek abu-abu dengan berkata: "You're different. You are not yellow but gray and brave." Ini menunjukkan kasih sayang seorang ibu yang menerima perbedaan anaknya.

distractorWhy.1: Mother Duck tidak mengusirnya; ia justru membela dan menenangkannya dari cemoohan bebek lain.
distractorWhy.2: Mother Duck tidak marah dan tetap menghitung serta merawat semua anak bebeknya.
distractorWhy.3: Mother Duck tidak mengabaikan anak bebek abu-abu tersebut, melainkan mengajaknya berenang bersama anak-anak bebek lainnya.

items.prompt: Dalam teks naratif seperti cerita The Ugly Duckling (halaman 103-105), kata kerja bentuk lampau (past tense action verbs) digunakan untuk menyatakan kejadian yang sudah terjadi. Manakah pasangan kata kerja bentuk lampau yang tepat untuk melengkapi kalimat: "The gray duck _____ with a funny wobble, while a yellow duckling _____ his muddy wings."?
options: walked - shook
walk - shake
walks - shakes
walking - shaking

why.0: Kata "walked" (V2 dari walk) dan "shook" (V2 dari shake) adalah bentuk past tense yang tepat sesuai tata bahasa naratif dalam Worksheet 2.4/2.5.

distractorWhy.1: Kata "walk" dan "shake" merupakan bentuk kata kerja dasar (infinitive/V1), bukan past tense.
distractorWhy.2: Kata "walks" dan "shakes" merupakan bentuk simple present tense untuk subjek tunggal, bukan past tense.
distractorWhy.3: Kata "walking" dan "shaking" merupakan bentuk present participle (-ing) yang memerlukan to be untuk membentuk continuous tense.

items.prompt: Berdasarkan konteks cerita The Ugly Duckling Part 1 (halaman 95-99), di manakah latar tempat dan apa peristiwa pembuka (orientation) dalam cerita tersebut?
options: Di sarang bebek dekat kolam pada hari yang hangat, tempat telur-telur Mother Duck menetas menjadi empat bebek kuning dan satu bebek abu-abu.
Di tengah kota besar yang ramai, tempat burung-burung mencari sisa makanan di jalanan.
Di puncak gunung yang tinggi, tempat induk elang melatih anak-anaknya terbang.
Di dalam kandang peternakan, tempat ayam dan sapi berbincang-bincang mengenai kegiatan sehari-hari.

why.0: Orientation cerita mengenalkan latar tempat di dekat kolam pada musim panas/hari hangat saat telur-telur bebek menetas menjadi empat bebek kuning dan satu bebek abu-abu.

distractorWhy.1: Latar kota besar bukan lokasi cerita fabel The Ugly Duckling dalam buku teks ini.
distractorWhy.2: Cerita tidak berlatar di puncak gunung ataupun menceritakan induk elang.
distractorWhy.3: Kandang peternakan dengan percakapan ayam dan sapi bukan bagian dari orientation Part 1.

items.prompt: Pada cerita The Ugly Duckling Part 2 (halaman 115-117), mengapa si Ugly Duckling akhirnya memutuskan untuk terbang meninggalkan sarang dan pergi ke seberang sungai?
options: Karena ia merasa sedih dan tertekan akibat sering diejek dan ditolak karena perbedaannya.
Karena ia ingin berpetualang mencari harta karun rahasia di seberang sungai.
Karena disuruh oleh ibunya untuk mencari makanan tambahan bagi saudara-saudaranya.
Karena ingin menantang ayam-ayam dewasa dalam perlombaan terbang.

why.0: Ugly Duckling pergi karena tidak tahan dengan perlakuan buruk dan ejekan dari lingkungan sekitar yang memperlakukannya secara tidak adil hanya karena penampilannya berbeda.

distractorWhy.1: Tujuan kepindahannya bukan untuk mencari harta karun, melainkan karena rasa sedih atas penolakan.
distractorWhy.2: Ibunya tidak pernah menyuruhnya pergi mencari makanan di seberang sungai.
distractorWhy.3: Ia tidak berniat menantang siapa pun dalam perlombaan terbang.

items.prompt: Berdasarkan cerita The Ugly Duckling Part 3 (halaman 119-121), bagaimana perasaan si Ugly Duckling saat seekor anjing besar yang lapar tiba-tiba muncul di peternakan?
options: Ia merasa sangat ketakutan (terrified) dan cemas akan keselamatan nyawanya.
Ia merasa gembira dan antusias ingin mengajak anjing tersebut bermain.
Ia merasa marah dan berusaha menyerang anjing besar itu.
Ia merasa bangga dan memamerkan bulu abu-abunya kepada anjing tersebut.

why.0: Dalam Teks Part 3 dan Worksheet 2.10, dijelaskan bahwa saat anjing besar mendekat, Ugly Duckling merasa "terrified" (sangat ketakutan).

distractorWhy.1: Perasaan gembira bertentangan dengan situasi ancaman bahaya dari anjing lapar.
distractorWhy.2: Ugly Duckling tidak bersikap agresif atau menyerang anjing tersebut.
distractorWhy.3: Ia tidak merasa bangga; ia bersembunyi ketakutan.

items.prompt: Nilai moral utama apakah yang dapat dipetik dari perubahan Ugly Duckling menjadi seekor angsa putih yang anggun (beautiful swan) di akhir cerita (halaman 121-123)?
options: Keindahan dan harga diri sejati berasal dari dalam diri, dan kita tidak boleh menilai seseorang hanya dari fisik luar atau penampilan awalnya.
Melarikan diri dari rumah adalah cara terbaik untuk menyelesaikan setiap masalah pribadi.
Menjadi berbeda secara fisik menjamin bahwa semua orang akan langsung mengagumi kita sejak awal.
Penampilan luar adalah satu-satunya hal yang menentukan karakter dan kebaikan seseorang.

why.0: Pesan moral utama fabel ini mengajarkan agar kita menghargai perbedaan dan tidak menghakimi seseorang berdasarkan rupa fisik semata.

distractorWhy.1: Melarikan diri bukanlah solusi utama yang diajarkan, melainkan ketabahan dan penemuan jati diri.
distractorWhy.2: Perbedaan fisik dalam cerita justru sempat membuat Ugly Duckling dimusuhi sebelum ia tumbuh dewasa.
distractorWhy.3: Penampilan luar bukan satu-satunya penentu karakter; kebaikan hati dan ketabahan jauh lebih utama.

items.prompt: Kalimat langsung (direct speech) ditandai dengan penggunaan tanda petik untuk mengutip ucapan tokoh secara persis. Manakah contoh kalimat langsung yang tepat sesuai teks cerita di Chapter 2?
options: "Can I please stay here?" asked the Ugly Duckling softly.
The Ugly Duckling asked if he could stay there softly.
Mother Duck told everyone that the gray duckling was brave.
The animals said that the tiger was very scary.

why.0: Kalimat "Can I please stay here?" asked the Ugly Duckling softly merupakan contoh direct speech karena mengutip ucapan langsung tokoh di dalam tanda petik.

distractorWhy.1: Kalimat tersebut merupakan kalimat tidak langsung (indirect/reported speech).
distractorWhy.2: Kalimat tersebut merupakan struktur indirect speech yang melaporkan pernyataan Mother Duck.
distractorWhy.3: Kalimat tersebut merupakan bentuk indirect speech tanpa tanda petik pengutip dialog.

items.prompt: Dalam cerita Elephant and Friends pada Chapter 2 Unit 3 (halaman 131-133), bagian manakah yang berfungsi sebagai Orientation (pengenalan cerita)?
options: Suatu hari seekor gajah mengembara di hutan untuk mencari teman dan bertemu seekor monyet di atas pohon.
Harimau mulai mengejar dan berusaha melahap semua hewan di dalam hutan.
Gajah menendang harimau hingga lari ketakutan dan menyelamatkan seluruh penghuni hutan.
Semua hewan akhirnya sepakat bahwa ukuran tubuh gajah sangat pas untuk menjadi teman mereka.

why.0: Orientation berisikan pengenalan tokoh (gajah, monyet), waktu (suatu hari), dan tempat (hutan) saat gajah mulai mencari teman.

distractorWhy.1: Peristiwa munculnya harimau mengejar hewan adalah bagian Complication (masalah).
distractorWhy.2: Tindakan gajah menendang harimau merupakan bagian Resolution (penyelesaian).
distractorWhy.3: Kesepakatan akhir hewan-hewan menerima gajah adalah penutup/Resolution dari cerita.

items.prompt: Berdasarkan percakapan pada halaman 133, apa alasan monyet menolak permintaan gajah untuk menjadi temannya?
options: Monyet menganggap gajah terlalu besar dan tidak bisa berayun di pohon seperti dirinya.
Monyet menganggap gajah terlalu kecil sehingga tidak bisa memanjat pohon tinggi.
Monyet takut gajah akan menghabiskan pisang persediaannya di hutan.
Monyet marah karena gajah tidak menyapanya dengan sopan.

why.0: Monyet yang sombong menjawab: "You are too big. You cannot swing from trees like me," yang menegaskan alasannya menolak gajah karena ukuran fisiknya.

distractorWhy.1: Monyet menolak karena tubuh gajah terlalu besar, bukan terlalu kecil.
distractorWhy.2: Dalam teks tidak disebutkan alasan mengenai makanan atau pisang.
distractorWhy.3: Gajah menyapa dengan sopan ("Will you be my friend?"), namun monyet menolaknya karena keangkuhannya.

items.prompt: Selain monyet, kelinci dan katak juga menolak menjadi teman gajah (halaman 133). Apakah alasan serupa yang disampaikan oleh kelinci dan katak tersebut?
options: Mereka menganggap tubuh gajah yang terlalu besar menghalanginya untuk beraktivitas bersama seperti masuk ke liang atau melompat.
Mereka menilai gajah merupakan hewan yang terlalu pendiam dan membosankan.
Mereka marah karena gajah telah merusak tempat tinggal mereka secara tidak sengaja.
Mereka hanya ingin berteman dengan hewan yang bisa terbang di udara.

why.0: Kelinci beralasan gajah terlalu besar untuk masuk ke liangnya ("too big to play in my burrow"), dan katak beralasan gajah terlalu besar untuk melompat ("too big to leap about").

distractorWhy.1: Alasan penolakan murni karena ukuran fisik tubuh gajah, bukan karena kepribadian pendiam.
distractorWhy.2: Gajah tidak merusak tempat tinggal kelinci maupun katak.
distractorWhy.3: Kelinci dan katak tidak menyebutkan syarat berteman hanya dengan hewan yang bisa terbang.

items.prompt: Masalah utama (Complication) apa yang terjadi di hutan pada hari berikutnya dalam cerita Elephant and Friends (halaman 134)?
options: Seekor harimau ganas mengancam keselamatan seluruh hewan dengan mencoba memangsa mereka.
Banjir bandang meluap dan menghancurkan semua pepohonan serta liang tempat tinggal hewan.
Gajah tersesat di dalam hutan dan tidak bisa menemukan jalan pulang.
Terjadi perselisihan besar antar-hewan untuk menentukan siapa peminpin hutan.

why.0: Complication muncul ketika harimau datang dan memangsa hewan-hewan hutan sehingga semua hewan berlarian menyelamatkan diri ("There is a tiger in the forest. He's trying to gobble us all up!").

distractorWhy.1: Bencana banjir tidak pernah diceritakan dalam teks fabel ini.
distractorWhy.2: Masalah utama bukan gajah tersesat, melainkan ancaman dari harimau.
distractorWhy.3: Tidak ada perebutan kepemimpinan hutan antar-hewan dalam cerita tersebut.

items.prompt: Bagaimana cara gajah menyelesaikan masalah (Resolution) dan menyelamatkan hewan-hewan lain dari ancaman harimau (halaman 134)?
options: Gajah dengan berani berjalan mendekati harimau, memintanya berhenti, lalu memberikan tendangan keras hingga harimau lari ketakutan.
Gajah berlari cepat dan bersembunyi di dalam goa yang dalam bersama kelinci.
Gajah meminta bantuan monyet untuk melemparkan buah kelapa ke arah harimau dari atas pohon.
Gajah membujuk harimau untuk menjadi vegetarian dan memakan rumput.

why.0: Gajah menemui harimau, memperingatkannya, dan ketika harimau menolak, gajah memberikan tendangan kuat ("hefty kick") hingga harimau melarikan diri.

distractorWhy.1: Gajah tidak bersembunyi; ia justru berdiri membela hewan-hewan lain.
distractorWhy.2: Gajah bertindak sendiri tanpa meminta monyet melemparkan kelapa.
distractorWhy.3: Gajah tidak membujuk harimau makan rumput, melainkan melawannya secara fisik.

items.prompt: Pada bagian penjelasan karakter (halaman 137), kata sifat (adjectives) digunakan untuk menggambarkan sifat tokoh. Manakah urutan kata sifat yang paling tepat untuk menggambarkan watak monyet, kelinci, dan katak sebelum datangnya ancaman harimau?
options: Arrogant (sombong), shy (pemalu), dan disgruntled (kesal/jengkel).
Generous (dermawan), brave (berani), dan humble (rendah hati).
Lazy (pemalas), polite (sopan), dan helpful (suka menolong).
Fierce (galak), dishonest (curang), dan cruel (kejam).

why.0: Dalam Teks Halaman 133 dan 137, monyet disebut "arrogant monkey", kelinci disebut "shy rabbit", dan katak disebut "disgruntled frog".

distractorWhy.1: Ketiga sifat tersebut bertolak belakang dengan sikap awal ketiga hewan yang menolak berteman.
distractorWhy.2: Ketiga hewan tersebut tidak ditunjukkan sebagai pemalas atau bersikap sopan pada gajah.
distractorWhy.3: Fierce dan cruel adalah sifat harimau, bukan monyet, kelinci, atau katak.

items.prompt: Pesan moral apakah yang disampaikan di akhir cerita Elephant and Friends ketika hewan-hewan berkata: "You are just the right size to be our friend!" (halaman 134-135)?
options: Pertemanan sejati diukur dari kebaikan hati dan kesediaan membantu sesama, bukan dari ukuran atau penampilan fisik.
Hanya hewan yang berbadan besar dan kuat yang layak memiliki banyak teman di hutan.
Kita hanya perlu membantu orang lain yang pernah bersikap baik kepada kita di masa lalu.
Hewan berukuran kecil selalu lebih cerdas daripada hewan berukuran besar.

why.0: Pesan moral fabel menekankan bahwa persahabatan tidak memandang fisik. Gajah yang tadinya ditolak karena terlalu besar akhirnya diterima karena kebaikan hati dan keberaniannya membantu.

distractorWhy.1: Pernyataan ini salah karena ukuran fisik bukan syarat utama pertemanan.
distractorWhy.2: Gajah tetap menolong hewan-hewan meskipun sebelumnya mereka menolaknya, mengajarkan kebaikan tanpa pamrih.
distractorWhy.3: Cerita tidak membandingkan kecerdasan berdasarkan ukuran tubuh.

items.prompt: Berdasarkan Word Box pada halaman 132, manakah kelompok kata kerja tak beraturan (irregular verbs) yang semuanya dalam bentuk past tense (V2) secara tepat?
options: saw, hid, leapt, flew, came
seed, hided, leaped, flyed, comed
seeing, hiding, leaping, flying, coming
sees, hides, leaps, flies, comes

why.0: Kata saw (dari see), hid (dari hide), leapt (dari leap), flew (dari fly), dan came (dari come) adalah bentuk past tense irregular verbs yang benar.

distractorWhy.1: Bentuk dengan akhiran -ed pada kata-kata tersebut salah karena kata-kata tersebut termasuk irregular verbs.
distractorWhy.2: Bentuk berakhiran -ing adalah present participle, bukan past tense (V2).
distractorWhy.3: Bentuk dengan s/es adalah simple present tense untuk subjek orang ketiga tunggal.

items.prompt: Berdasarkan tabel struktur teks naratif pada halaman 140-143, apakah fungsi utama dari bagian Complication dalam sebuah cerita fabel?
options: Memaparkan konflik, tantangan, atau masalah utama yang dihadapi oleh para tokoh.
Memperkenalkan tokoh, latar tempat, dan latar waktu terjadinya peristiwa.
Memberikan penyelesaian atau solusi atas masalah yang terjadi.
Menyampaikan pesan moral secara tertulis dalam bentuk daftar poin di akhir teks.

why.0: Sesuai penjelasan struktur teks naratif di halaman 141-143, Complication berfungsi "Showing the conflict(s) or problem(s) in the story".

distractorWhy.1: Fungsi memperkenalkan tokoh dan latar adalah milik bagian Orientation.
distractorWhy.2: Fungsi memberikan penyelesaian adalah milik bagian Resolution.
distractorWhy.3: Pesan moral terintegrasi dalam cerita atau re-orientation, bukan fungsi utama complication.

items.prompt: Perhatikan kalimat langsung berikut: The elephant asked, "Will you be my friend?". Manakah bentuk kalimat tidak langsung (indirect speech) yang tepat dari kalimat tersebut?
options: The elephant asked if the animal would be his friend.
The elephant says that you will be my friend.
The elephant ask will you be my friend yesterday.
The elephant is asking to be friends right now.

why.0: Pengubahan direct speech berupa yes/no question memakai kata hubung "if", tenses berubah menjadi past (will -> would), dan kata ganti disesuaikan (you -> the animal/he, my -> his).

distractorWhy.1: Kata kerja reporting verb "says" menggunakan present tense dan kata ganti tidak disesuaikan.
distractorWhy.2: Kata kerja "ask" tidak beraturan (kurang -ed) dan struktur tanda petik tidak diubah.
distractorWhy.3: Penggunaan present continuous tense ("is asking") tidak sesuai dengan pengubahan past narrative.

items.prompt: Dalam cerita Elephant and Friends (halaman 134), terdapat kalimat: "The elephant wondered what he could do to save everyone in the forest." Kata sifat (adjective) manakah yang paling tepat untuk menggambarkan karakter gajah berdasarkan tindakan tersebut?
options: Brave (berani) dan compassionate (bela rasa/peduli).
Arrogant (sombong) dan greedy (serakah).
Cowardly (penakut) dan selfish (egois).
Indifferent (cuek) dan lazy (pemalas).

why.0: Tindakan gajah yang memikirkan keselamatan hewan lain dan menghadapi harimau mencerminkan sifat berani (brave) serta peduli/bela rasa (compassionate).

distractorWhy.1: Gajah tidak sombong ataupun serakah; ia justru rendah hati dan mau berbagi.
distractorWhy.2: Gajah tidak penakut atau egois karena ia bertindak menyelamatkan hewan lain.
distractorWhy.3: Gajah sangat peduli dan aktif bergerak, bukan acuh tak acuh atau pemalas.

items.prompt: Chapter 2 memiliki judul utama "Kindness Begins with Me". Apakah benang merah (tema utama) yang menghubungkan cerita The Ugly Duckling dan Elephant and Friends?
options: Menunjukkan kebaikan hati dan kepedulian terhadap sesama tanpa memandang perbedaan fisik akan membawa kedamaian dan pertemanan sejati.
Saling bersaing untuk membuktikan siapa hewan terkuat dan paling indah di dalam hutan.
Prinsip bertahan hidup di mana hanya hewan berpenampilan menarik yang berhak bahagia.
Menjauhi semua interaksi dengan hewan lain yang berbeda spesies untuk menghindari masalah.

why.0: Kedua cerita mengusung sub-tema Kindness towards Differences dan Kindness and Friendship, menegaskan bahwa kebaikan hati mengatasi segala perbedaan fisik.

distractorWhy.1: Persaingan dan adu kekuatan bukan tema yang diangkat dalam Chapter 2.
distractorWhy.2: Teks justru menolak anggapan bahwa hanya hewan menarik yang berhak bahagia.
distractorWhy.3: Teks mendorong interaksi dan kebaikan antar-spesies/hewan yang berbeda.

items.prompt: Dalam penulisan naratif, dua kejadian di masa lalu dapat dihubungkan menggunakan Past Continuous Tense dan Simple Past Tense. Lengkapilah kalimat berikut: "While the other animals _____ in fear, the elephant _____ forward to face the tiger."
options: were hiding - stepped
are hiding - steps
hide - step
will hide - will step

why.0: Klausa "While..." menyatakan tindakan yang sedang berlangsung di masa lalu menggunakan past continuous (were hiding), disusul tindakan selingan dalam simple past (stepped).

distractorWhy.1: Bentuk "are hiding" dan "steps" menggunakan present tense, tidak cocok untuk konteks teks naratif lampau.
distractorWhy.2: Bentuk "hide" dan "step" menggunakan verb 1 (present), bukan past tense.
distractorWhy.3: Bentuk "will hide" dan "will step" menggunakan future tense untuk kejadian di masa depan.

competencies.name: Chapter 3: Love Our World
competencies.materi: Environmental Conservation Texts, Reducing Plastic Waste, Procedural Posters & Tips, Imperative Expressions for Saving Water/Energy
competencies.cpRef: English for Nusantara untuk SMP/MTs Kelas VII — Chapter 3 (Kelas VIII)

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 157-159 Unit 1 Comic Strip 3.1), what causes the trash bin at the school canteen to overflow?
options: Plastic waste from snack wrappers and straws
Overflowing paper waste from old school notebooks
Leftover organic food waste from the school kitchen
Broken glass bottles and discarded aluminium cans

why.0: The trash bin at the canteen overflows mainly because it is filled with plastic waste from snack wrappers and straws.

distractorWhy.1: Notebook paper waste is not mentioned as filling the canteen trash bin.
distractorWhy.2: Kitchen organic food waste is not the primary cause stated in the text.
distractorWhy.3: Glass bottles and aluminium cans are not mentioned in Comic Strip 3.1.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 158 Unit 1 Comic Strip 3.1), what action do Monita and Andre decide to take for their future canteen lunches to reduce plastic waste?
options: Bring their own food containers from home
Buy more packaged snacks with plastic straws
Ask the canteen sellers to use single-use paper bags
Throw their plastic trash in another school bin

why.0: Monita suggests bringing their own food containers next time to avoid generating plastic wrapper waste.

distractorWhy.1: Buying more packaged snacks increases plastic consumption.
distractorWhy.2: Asking canteen sellers for paper bags is not the specific action agreed upon.
distractorWhy.3: Throwing trash elsewhere does not reduce overall plastic usage.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 159 Unit 1 Worksheet 3.2), what does Monita mean when she says "Good idea, Andre!"?
options: She agrees with Andre's suggestion to reduce plastic waste
She thinks Andre should buy more snacks at the canteen
She wants Andre to clean the canteen trash bin by himself
She doubts whether reducing plastic waste will help the environment

why.0: "Good idea" expresses agreement with Andre's proposal to bring food containers from home to reduce plastic waste.

distractorWhy.1: Buying more snacks contradicts the idea of reducing waste.
distractorWhy.2: She is not instructing Andre to clean the trash bin.
distractorWhy.3: She fully supports saving the environment rather than doubting it.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 160-163 Unit 1 Handwashing Procedure), what is the proper action regarding the water faucet while rubbing hands with soap?
options: Turn off the faucet while rubbing hands to save water
Keep the faucet running continuously throughout handwashing
Increase the water flow to rinse the soap faster
Splash water onto the floor to keep hands wet

why.0: The procedure specifies turning off the faucet while rubbing hands with soap so water is not wasted.

distractorWhy.1: Leaving the faucet running wastes clean water needlessly.
distractorWhy.2: Increasing water flow while soaping is wasteful.
distractorWhy.3: Splashing water on the floor is improper and unhygienic.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 163 Unit 1 Did You Know section), what common health problem is caused by unhygienic water and unsafe sanitation?
options: Diarrhea
Influenza
Asthma
Tooth decay

why.0: Unhygienic water and poor sanitation frequently cause diarrhea, which can prevent children from attending school.

distractorWhy.1: Influenza is an airborne viral respiratory disease.
distractorWhy.2: Asthma is a chronic respiratory condition unrelated to water sanitation.
distractorWhy.3: Tooth decay is related to dental hygiene and diet rather than waterborne pathogens.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 164 Unit 1 Language Focus Table 3.2), which expression is appropriate for the "Showing the steps" stage of a procedural presentation?
options: First, turn on the faucet and wash our hands with running water.
Good afternoon everyone, my name is Alifandra.
I am going to show you how to wash our hands without wasting water.
Thank you very much for your kind attention.

why.0: "First, ..." is a sequential transition marker used to present procedural steps.

distractorWhy.1: This expression belongs to the starting the presentation stage.
distractorWhy.2: This expression belongs to the stating the goal stage.
distractorWhy.3: This expression belongs to the ending the presentation stage.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 166-168 Unit 1 Comic Strip 3.3), why does Galang remind Pipit while she is washing her hands?
options: Because Pipit left the faucet running while rubbing her hands with soap
Because Pipit forgot to use soap when washing her hands
Because Pipit rubbed her hands for only five seconds
Because Pipit used dirty river water instead of tap water

why.0: Galang points out that leaving the tap running while soaping hands wastes precious water.

distractorWhy.1: Pipit was using soap, but left the water running.
distractorWhy.2: Pipit was rubbing her hands for 60 seconds.
distractorWhy.3: Pipit was using tap water at school.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 174-175 Unit 2 Comic Strip 3.4), what topic is discussed in the social media post that Monita shares with her friends?
options: Sorting trash to help save the earth
Playing online video games on weekends
Ordering fast food online for school lunch
Buying fashion items on discount sales

why.0: Monita shares a social media post written by a girl about how to sort household trash to save the environment.

distractorWhy.1: Video games are not mentioned in Monita's post.
distractorWhy.2: Fast food delivery is unrelated to the environmental post.
distractorWhy.3: Online shopping is not the topic of the post.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 178-179 Unit 2 Picture 3.3 Language Focus), what should we do before commenting on social media?
options: Read and understand the content carefully, then think if we have something necessary and polite to offer
Post immediate emotional reactions without reading the whole text
Use aggressive words to win arguments in the comment section
Share private personal phone numbers and home addresses publicly

why.0: Responsible social media etiquette requires reading carefully and commenting politely only when offering necessary, constructive thoughts.

distractorWhy.1: Reacting emotionally without reading causes misunderstanding.
distractorWhy.2: Aggressive words spark unnecessary quarrels.
distractorWhy.3: Sharing private details online compromises personal safety.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 180 Unit 2 Internet Safety Rules), which practice is recommended for staying safe online?
options: Do not share personal information such as home address and phone number online
Download files freely from unknown and suspicious websites
Trust anyone you meet on social media right away
Post negative comments to criticise classmates publicly

why.0: Protecting privacy by withholding home address and phone number is a core rule for online safety.

distractorWhy.1: Downloading from suspicious sites exposes devices to malware.
distractorWhy.2: Trusting strangers online poses serious safety risks.
distractorWhy.3: Posting hurtful content constitutes cyberbullying.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 183-184 Unit 2 Section 6), what main problem does @in22day express in the social media post?
options: Having too many old books in the room that are no longer read
Lacking money to buy school textbooks
Losing an important library book at school
Wanting to build a commercial bookstore in town

why.0: @in22day asks friends for advice on what to do with accumulated old books that are no longer read.

distractorWhy.1: Lacking money is not @in22day's expressed problem.
distractorWhy.2: No mention of losing a school library book.
distractorWhy.3: @in22day is seeking ways to manage personal unused books, not starting a commercial business.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 183-184 Unit 2 Worksheet 3.14), what is the first step to donate old books to Bina Karya orphanage according to @titalesta?
options: Fill in the donation form on the provided website link
Send the books directly by post without filling out any form
Sell the books at Palasari Market first
Cover the books with plastic layers

why.0: @titalesta states: "First fill in the form in the link www.binakaryadonation.com".

distractorWhy.1: Sending books before filling out the online form misses the required initial step.
distractorWhy.2: Selling books at Palasari Market is @zalvafsp's suggestion, not @titalesta's donation step.
distractorWhy.3: Covering books with plastic is part of @zalvafsp's selling procedure.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 183-184 Unit 2 Section 6), which commenter gives a response that is not related to solving @in22day's problem with old books?
options: @shakila, who recommends watching movies
@agungibr, who suggests making a cardboard mini library
@titalesta, who invites book donations for an orphanage
@zalvafsp, who suggests selling good condition books at Palasari Market

why.0: @shakila's comment asks about movie recommendations, which does not address the issue of managing old books.

distractorWhy.1: @agungibr gives a detailed step-by-step method to build a mini bookshelf.
distractorWhy.2: @titalesta offers a clear donation channel for the books.
distractorWhy.3: @zalvafsp provides practical steps to resell unused books.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 187-193 Unit 3 Section 3), what are the two main elements of an instructional procedural poster?
options: Goal and Steps
Orientation and Reorientation
Complication and Resolution
Thesis and Arguments

why.0: Instructional procedural posters focus on communicating a clear Goal and procedural Steps.

distractorWhy.1: Orientation and Reorientation belong to recount or narrative text structures.
distractorWhy.2: Complication and Resolution belong to narrative texts.
distractorWhy.3: Thesis and Arguments belong to exposition texts.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 194-195 Unit 3 Language Focus Table 3.4), what visual effect do warm colors (ranging from yellow to reddish violet) create in poster design?
options: They appear to come forward, look larger, and are suitable for foreground elements
They appear to move backward, look smaller, and are suitable for background elements
They create a cold, quiet, and sad atmosphere exclusively
They make text unreadable and obscure all visual details

why.0: Warm colors make visual elements come forward and look larger, making them ideal for foreground emphasis.

distractorWhy.1: Moving backward and looking smaller is the visual effect of cool colors.
distractorWhy.2: Cold, quiet, and sad moods are associated with cool colors.
distractorWhy.3: Warm colors are strategically used to draw attention, not obscure details.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 195 Unit 3 Table 3.4), how is an analogous color combination formed on a color wheel for poster creation?
options: By combining colors that are next to each other on the color wheel, such as sky blue, green, and yellowish green
By combining colors directly opposite each other on the color wheel, such as yellow and violet
By combining dark black and pure white without any hues
By selecting random colors with no spatial relationship on the wheel

why.0: Analogous color schemes use adjacent colors on the color wheel to create harmonious visual balance.

distractorWhy.1: Combining opposite colors forms a complementary color scheme.
distractorWhy.2: Black and white form a monochromatic/achromatic contrast, not analogous hues.
distractorWhy.3: Analogous combinations follow strict adjacency rules on the color wheel.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 196 Unit 3 Table 3.4), what visual characteristic distinguishes a complementary color combination (e.g., yellow and violet)?
options: Striking contrast between opposite colors on the color wheel
Subtle, calm, and invisible blending of identical tones
Monochrome grayscale without any bright highlights
Smooth pastel shades with zero visual impact

why.0: Complementary colors sit opposite each other on the color wheel, producing high-contrast, striking visuals.

distractorWhy.1: Identical tones lack the high contrast of complementary pairs.
distractorWhy.2: Grayscale does not describe chromatic complementary color pairs.
distractorWhy.3: Complementary colors produce striking visual impact rather than zero impact.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 197 Unit 3 Table 3.5), what is the main purpose of adding illustrations to an environmental procedural poster?
options: To clarify and represent the intended procedural steps visually
To fill all blank spaces so that no text can be read
To decorate the poster with unrelated cartoon characters
To hide the main goal of the poster from readers

why.0: Illustrations in posters complement the text, making the procedural steps clear and engaging.

distractorWhy.1: Overcrowding blank space makes posters unreadable.
distractorWhy.2: Unrelated decorative images distract from the poster's key message.
distractorWhy.3: Illustrations should clarify the main goal, not hide it.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (page 198 Unit 3 Section 5 Fun Time), what word in the crossword puzzle corresponds to the clue "the thing that runs water"?
options: Faucet
Towel
Soap
Poster

why.0: A faucet is the plumbing fixture that controls and supplies running water.

distractorWhy.1: A towel is used for drying hands.
distractorWhy.2: Soap is used for cleansing.
distractorWhy.3: A poster is a printed paper or cardboard displaying information.

items.prompt: Based on English for Nusantara Grade VIII (pages 160 and 190 Imperative Expressions), which sentence correctly uses an imperative form to instruct someone to conserve water when washing hands?
options: Turn off the faucet while rubbing your hands with soap.
You are turning off the faucet right now.
Did you turn off the faucet after washing?
The faucet was turned off by Galang.

why.0: "Turn off..." is a direct imperative sentence starting with a base verb to give clear procedural instructions.

distractorWhy.1: This is a present continuous declarative sentence.
distractorWhy.2: This is a past tense interrogative sentence.
distractorWhy.3: This is a passive voice sentence in the simple past tense.

competencies.name: Chapter 4: No Littering
competencies.materi: Recounting Waste Clean-Up Events, Waste Sorting & Management, Past Continuous Tense (was/were + v-ing), Environmental Action
